subject: biology
title: From Cells to Organisms
welcome_lead: Discover how tiny cells team up to build tissues, organs and entire living bodies.
meta_desc: KS3 Biology adventure on levels of organisation from cells to whole organisms.
final_note: You can now climb the ladder of organisation from a single cell to a full organism.

concepts.def: Smallest unit of a living organism.
Group of similar cells doing one job.
Group of organs that share a function.
A cell shaped for a particular job.

walkthroughs.body_html: Cells form tissues, tissues form organs, organs form organ systems, and systems together form an organism. Each level builds on the one below.
Muscle cells form muscle tissue, which forms the heart (an organ). The heart is part of the circulatory system, which works with other systems to make a human organism.
Different jobs need different shapes. A red blood cell is small and flat to carry oxygen; a nerve cell is long to send signals. Specialised cells make tissues efficient.
